_comment: Reduced-scale version of paper Fig. 5 (parametric softmax vs growing weighted softmax: train-test gap) on a CPU, since the A100 run was lost. 5,000 training images (first 5,000 of the Hugging Face order), augmentation, batch 64, L = 0 (one readout layer on RMSNorm'd pixels). GWS: 40 epochs (199,744 stored rows; eta = 0.003, beta = 10, T = 10 as in multi_epoch.json). Parametric softmax: 10,000 trained keys and values (2 per training image), Adam 1e-3, 100 epochs, T = 1 and 0.1. Paper: 2.56M trained keys for 50,000 images, 2,000 epochs; GWS 50 epochs. Train accuracy is measured on the first 2,000 (non-augmented) training images, test accuracy on the first 2,000 test images (final: all 10,000). The parametric softmax uses fixed equal weights (plain softmax), as the paper reports for this baseline (App. E.4: learned weights 'lead to severe training instabilities'); with learned weights the T = 1 run diverged at step ~1,500 here.
